record.paper_title: Mapping current and activity fluctuations in exclusion processes: consequences and open questions
record.context_brief: Relation to other exclusion-process large-deviation mappings
record.original_question: Can the similarity-transform mapping between the joint scaled cumulant generating functions of current and activity in ASEP models be related to previously known mappings for current large-deviation functions or for steady-state large deviations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) on a one-dimensional periodic lattice of L sites with hard-core particles that hop right with rate p and left with rate q, subject to the exclusion rule that each site contains at most one particle. For a long time window [0,T], let Q_T denote the time-integrated current (number of right jumps minus left jumps across a fixed bond, or summed over all bonds) and K_T the time-integrated activity (total number of jumps, regardless of direction). Define the joint scaled cumulant generating function

  ψ(λ, μ) = lim_{T→∞} (1/T) log ⟨ exp( λ Q_T + μ K_T ) ⟩,

which can be obtained as the largest eigenvalue of the tilted (deformed) Markov generator W(λ, μ) acting on configuration space. It is known that there exists a similarity transformation W'(λ', μ') = U W(λ, μ) U^{-1} relating the tilted generators of two ASEPs with possibly different hopping rates and tilting parameters, thereby producing an exact mapping between their joint current–activity scaled cumulant generating functions, and in particular relating current large deviations in the ASEP to activity large deviations in the symmetric simple exclusion process (SSEP).

Question: Can this similarity-transform mapping between joint current–activity scaled cumulant generating functions of ASEP-type models be derived from, or otherwise put into precise correspondence with, the previously established mappings between current large-deviation functions of exclusion processes (such as those relating ASEP and zero-range or related processes via gauge-type transformations) and the mappings used in the analysis of steady-state large deviations of exclusion processes (e.g., via matrix-product or additivity-principle techniques)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open direction in the literature on mapping current and activity fluctuations in exclusion processes; web search did not surface any subsequent work establishing a precise relation between the similarity-transform mapping for joint current–activity SCGFs and the earlier mappings for current LDFs or steady-state large deviations. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: Establishes a similarity-transform mapping between joint current-activity SCGFs of ASEPs and asks whether it can be related to known mappings for current LDFs or steady-state large deviations.
status_evidence.claim: The relation to previously known current-LDF and steady-state LDF mappings is raised as an open question.
